# Vendored, never edited

## `ed25519_bams.py`
A **byte-for-byte copy** of `server/ed25519.py` from `coolman1984/Mr.Ayman-HR` (BAMS) at commit `5f5b3ce`,
SHA-256 `cb772f845301e8b81baaec496910c778526919b37061e8e6c6b05489ed9cdd1b`.

- It is the **fallback** signing backend only (ADR-HR-002 in `docs/HR_SECURITY.md`): HR prefers the standard
  `cryptography` package (OpenSSL) whenever it can be imported.
- **Do not edit this file.** `TEST_HR_SECURITY.py` fails if its SHA-256 changes. A fix belongs in BAMS (its owner),
  then the new version is copied here unchanged and the pinned hash updated — there is never a second, independently
  modified copy of a security algorithm. Long term it moves to the shared ecosystem foundation (GMES docs/ecosystem/08).
- Reviewed 2026-09-27: RFC 8032 §5.1 algorithms; verification is cofactorless (`[s]B = R + [k]A`), rejects `s >= q`
  (malleability) and non-canonical `y`; signing is not constant-time (documented in the file; outside the LAN threat model).
  Proven by RFC 8032 test vectors, cross-checks against two independent implementations (`cryptography` in both
  directions, and the OpenSSL command line), and mutation tests (`TEST_HR_SECURITY.py`, `migration/mutations.py`).
